extracted.intended_audience: students and practitioners of classical/geometric quadrature (mathematicians or geometry students reading an older Italian treatise)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural rules and heuristics for computing areas and surfaces (quadrature) and volumes of regular solids, pyramids, cones, spheres, and divisions of those surfaces; includes numeric recipes, use of inscribed/circumscribed polygons, and practical measurement advice. The page is an excerpt from an older Italian geometry treatise giving stepwise operations (multiply, divide, extract roots) and worked numeric examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quadratura dei corpi regolari (quadrature of regular solids)
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedure for finding the surface (and parts) of regular polyhedra: obtain the face area from a given diameter/side and then multiply by the number of faces to get the solid's total surface. (Original phrasing: 'Corporibua rcplaribue' / 'Corporibus regularibus'.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute the area of one regular face (triangular equilateral, square, etc.) from the given linear measure (diameter or side) using the indicated multiplications and extractions; then multiply that face-area by the count of faces. The text gives numerous numeric examples and specific factor manipulations (e.g. working with powers like 64, 4096 and multiplying by face counts). Follow the stepwise numeric recipes shown in the examples rather than assuming modern formulas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quadratura delle facce triangolari equilateri (area from side or diameter for equilateral triangular faces)
rubrics_metrics.description: When faces are equilateral triangles, convert the given diameter/side into the triangle's side and find its area; several worked numeric recipes show how to obtain the triangle area and then use it in the solid's surface. (Original references: 'triangulare equilatero', 'la fupfìa cbe fa la...')
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extract or compute the required ratio from diameter to side (the treatise repeatedly indicates dividing and multiplying by specific factors), square or otherwise manipulate those measures per example, then sum/multiply per number of faces. The page contains explicit step-by-step numeric cases (including checking by dividing into parts and recombining).

rubrics_metrics.name: Quadratura di sfere (sphere surface quadrature by relation to circles/polygons)
rubrics_metrics.description: Methods to obtain the quadrature (surface and related measures) of a sphere by relating its diameter and surface to circle(s) and to inscribed/circumscribed polygons. The text repeatedly compares the sphere's surface to circle-cases and prescribes proportional arithmetic operations. (Original phrasing: 'fupfidcdiqlla fpa... la radici', 'la fupfidc de la pomde de la fpera').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the diameter, consider corresponding circles/circumferences, and apply multiplications and extraction of roots as directed to get area measures. The treatise emphasizes dividing the sphere's surface into portions, comparing to circle areas, using successive multiplications and roots (including cube and square roots) and numeric examples to reach the quadrature. It also discusses approximating the sphere via polygons and using proportions with circumscribed/circumference relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quadratura di piramidi e coni (quadrature of pyramids and cones)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for 'squaring' (finding an equivalent planar area or related measure) of pyramids and cones by reducing to known quadratures or constructing auxiliary solids. (Original hints: 'prima quadrare la piramide', 'quadrare la piramide dx fai...')
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text prescribes first reducing the pyramid/cone to an associated solid (e.g., produce a sphere or other figure whose quadrature is known), using base and height relations, and then applying multiplicative steps and partitions shown in examples. Follow the recipe-like instructions (partition base, take proportional parts, multiply/divide) from the examples rather than assuming a single modern formula; worked numeric sequences illustrate the intended operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approximation via inscribed/circumscribed polygons (use of multi‑gons to approach circle/sphere measures)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of inscribed and circumscribed polygons (multangoli / multiàg) and repeated doubling of sides to approximate circles and thereby approximate areas/surfaces. (Original phrasing: 'Piulnàg^ifcripta ... la fga p cb crypxefi', 'moltiplicalli... duplicando i lati').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replace the circle (or spherical section) by regular polygons with many sides; double the number of sides repeatedly to get closer approximations. The treatise explains how area/perimeter of these polygons converge and prescribes taking successive approximations (doubling sides, comparing perimeters/areas) and using those polygonal areas to estimate the circle/sphere measures. It also discusses complementing inscribed/circumscribed polygon results to bound the true value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divisione e ripartizione di superfici (dividing surfaces into equal or proportional parts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Instructions for dividing surfaces (faces, spherical zones, etc.) by taking diameters or lines and partitioning into proportional segments to compute parts' areas. (Original: 'prendere la diametro ... dividere ... pigliare la ragion')
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Take the given diameter or reference line, divide it into specified numbers of equal parts, then multiply/divide as directed to obtain the area of a portion. The page gives several numeric recipes for partitioning (e.g., divide into 2, 4, 8, 24 parts) and recombining to obtain areas of sectors, faces, and portions of solids.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arithmetic operations and numeric recipes (multiply, divide, extract square/cube roots)
rubrics_metrics.description: Emphasis on concrete arithmetic procedures: multiply given measures by specified factors, take square or cube roots, and use powers (e.g., 64, 4096) as intermediate steps in quadrature computations. (Original scattered numeric examples: '4096', '64', '32', '72', '79', etc.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the text's stepwise numeric manipulations: convert linear measures to powers or products, multiply by enumerated constants, and extract roots where called for. The treatise provides many worked numeric examples demonstrating how the operations are chained; these recipes are central to obtaining the claimed quadratures and should be applied exactly in analogous problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical measurement and experimental advice (measuring volumes by slicing, averaging)
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance for real-world measurement of volumes/areas (e.g., measuring a barrel — 'botte'): slice the solid, measure cross-sections, average multiple measures, and beware imperfect manufacture. (Original phrasing: 'misurare la botte ... tagliarla ... pigliare più misure ... non farsi ingannare dalle botti malfatte').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When applying theory to physical objects, cut or section the object to measure cross-sectional areas, average repeated measures, and use many slices to reduce error. The text warns against trusting poorly-made objects and recommends multiple independent measures and careful averaging; it also suggests building and measuring models when convenient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of proportional relations between face, diameter, and circumscribed circles
rubrics_metrics.description: Repeated use of proportional relationships: the face or portion area is expressed in proportion to a circle or to the diameter; many constructions use proportionality to go from diameters/lines to areas. (Original wording: 'la fupficie è la fpa ... nella circonferentia ... la ragion ... pigliare la parte')
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set up proportional relations between the given linear measures (diameter, side) and the target area, then compute by multiplying/dividing according to the given proportion. The treatise relies on these proportional steps to bridge from line measures to areas and surfaces; follow the examples converting diameters into corresponding planar measures via proportions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Caveats about approximation and practical limits (bounds, sensitivity to construction)
rubrics_metrics.description: Warnings that quadrature by polygons and practical measures gives approximations that can be made arbitrarily close by doubling/adding sides, but also remarks that small construction errors or imperfect objects (barrels, staves) can spoil measurements. (Original remarks: 'non è facile ... le botti mal fatte ... bisogna pigliare molte misure')
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When approximating, be aware of bounds (inscribed vs circumscribed) and improve precision by increasing polygon sides or measuring more cross-sections. For physical objects, compensate for manufacturing defects by multiple measures and careful instrument use. The treatise provides qualitative guidance and practical examples illustrating these limits.
